variables.name: TRON_HWATTN_EARLY_LAUNCH_MIN_B

readers.program: tron::init_hwattn_early_launch_min_b, header code compiled into the full scheduler library (rinzler, runtron, rinzler_host through fake_scheduler_static, model tests). Not in rinzler_proxy or rinzler_mock, which link other schedulers
readers.mechanism: getenv inside a function-local static, then strtoull base 10 with a digits-only check

readers.program: model::state::hw_attention_phase (the caller that uses the value)

variables.values: Positive decimal integer. Every character must be a digit 0-9. A sign, a space or a suffix is rejected. Leading zeros are accepted (04 means 4). The value must be at least 1 and must fit in 64 bits. Unit: token jobs in one minibatch (the batch size B, q_batch->items.size()).
variables.empty_value: Rejected like an invalid value: the process aborts at first use.
variables.invalid_value: TRON_ASSERT at h/tron/models/model.hpp:121-125 fails. The process writes the error log line 'TRON_ASSERT(...): invalid TRON_HWATTN_EARLY_LAUNCH_MIN_B '<value>'; expected a positive integer', then 'Aborting.', and calls std::abort (h/common/assert.hpp:59-63). Rejected inputs: empty text, a sign (+4, -1), a space, a letter, 0, and a number above the 64-bit range. The check runs at the first use. The first use is in a forward pass, when the first attention job is prepared (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2460-2461). It is not at program start. So a program with a bad value starts, loads the model, and aborts later.
variables.effect: Sets the smallest minibatch size that uses the early launch of hardware attention. A minibatch with at least this many token jobs prepares and launches hardware attention before the K/V saves of the current token. A smaller minibatch saves K/V first and then prepares and launches (Note at h/tron/models/model.hpp:95-109, select_hw_attention_launch_phase at h/tron/models/model.hpp:159-163). The value 1 means always early. A value above every batch size means always late.
variables.interactions: It selects only the launch time. It cannot make a software-only operation use hardware (h/tron/models/model.hpp:107-109). It matters only for operations that run on hardware attention. No command-line flag sets it.
variables.how_to_check: No log line prints the value. Perfetto trace instant events of the category hwattention-detail (early_hw_attn_prepare, early_hw_attn, late_hw_attn_prepare, late_hw_attn) carry the argument min_b with the value in effect (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2467-2469, :2580-2582, :2595-2597, :2614-2616).
variables.audience_reason: It is a performance tuning value of the inference path in rinzler and runtron. The default is right for normal use.
variables.disagreement: Vague, not wrong. cpp-tron.json says the process aborts 'on first use'. The code shows that the first use is in the first forward pass that prepares an attention job (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2460-2461, :2562-2563), not at program start. A server with a bad value starts and loads the model, then aborts when inference begins. The document should say this. All other fields agree.

variables.name: TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING

readers.program: libpos, the driver for real FPGA cards (rinzler, runtron, hardware tests). Not in pos_fake programs (rinzler_host, rinzler_mock, rinzler_proxy)
readers.mechanism: hwattn_env_override("TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING") in PosDevice::init. The result is kept in a function-local static
std::getenv(env_name), then std::atoi. The name is an argument, so a search for getenv with a quoted name does not find this variable

variables.values: Integer parsed with std::atoi. A result above 0 forces head tiling ON. Every other set value forces it OFF.
variables.default: Unset: each card decides from its bitfile (the FPGA image). hwattn_tiling_bitfile_ok returns true for project 01 or 03 with version 05.09 or later (h/pos/device.hpp:802-808).
variables.empty_value: atoi gives 0, so head tiling is forced OFF. This differs from unset.
variables.invalid_value: No error is reported. Non-numeric text gives 0, so words such as true, on or yes force the feature OFF. A negative number forces OFF. Text that starts with a positive number (for example 1x) forces ON.
variables.effect: Sets the flag attn_tiling_enabled of every card and skips the bitfile capability check (src/pos/device.cpp:219). With the flag on, an attention pass that covers more K/V shards than fit in EMEM in one pass is sent as one hardware command that handles fewer heads per K/V pass (hwattn_plan_cmd_shape, h/libpos.hpp:205-217, src/pos/worker.cpp:868-874). EMEM is the FPGA memory that holds the Q.K dot products of hardware attention (h/libpos.hpp:128-130). With the flag off, such a pass is split into several commands. The model planner uses the same flag (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2990-2992, :3057-3061).
variables.interactions: HWATTN_WLR is the sibling override, read by the same helper (src/pos/device.cpp:215). The flag matters only when hardware attention runs. A forced ON on a bitfile older than 05.09 skips the check that exists for the attention fixes named at h/pos/device.hpp:797-801. not determined: what the card does in that case (the code does not say). No command-line flag sets it.
variables.how_to_check: When the variable is set, the driver logs once at info level: 'HW attention: TRON_HWATTN_HEAD_TILING=<value> forces the feature ON|OFF by env flag; the bitfile capability check is bypassed' (src/pos/device.cpp:106-108). For every card, a debug log line at init prints 'caps { ... attn_tiling_enabled: true|false }' (src/pos/device.cpp:337, text built at h/pos/device.hpp:569-575). The debug line needs log level debug, which is the default of TRON_LOG_LEVEL.
variables.audience_reason: It overrides a hardware capability check and the default is automatic. A support engineer may still use the value 0 to turn head tiling off as a workaround.

variables.values: Exactly the text 1 or the text true turns the sampler on. The comparison is case-sensitive. Every other text is off (for example TRUE, yes, on, 2).
variables.default: Unset: off. No sampler thread is created, and a trace holds no counters of the category hw.
variables.invalid_value: Off. No error or warning is reported.
variables.effect: Turns on the hardware telemetry sampler. When a trace session starts, the process creates one background thread. While the trace records the category hw, the thread reads CPU temperature (hwmon), CPU frequency (cpufreq) and package power (RAPL) from sysfs and writes them to the trace as counters (src/pos/hwperf.cpp:598-633, :685-722). The thread pins itself to CPU 0 (src/pos/hwperf.cpp:642).
variables.interactions: It has an effect only when a trace session starts: runtron --trace, the SIGUSR1 timed trace, or a FUSE capture. TRON_HW_SAMPLER_INTERVAL_MS, TRON_HW_SAMPLER_ALL_SENSORS and TRON_HW_SAMPLER_SYSFS_ROOT tune the sampler and do nothing without it. The script perfetto/grant-rapl-read tests the same two values before it widens read access to the RAPL energy files (perfetto/grant-rapl-read:24). After the sampler thread exists, the variable is not read again. If the thread stops on an exception, it is not created again in that process (src/pos/hwperf.cpp:732-751).
variables.how_to_check: At its first recording tick the sampler logs at info level 'hw telemetry: cpu frequency sampled from N of M <source>' when cpufreq files exist (src/pos/hwperf.cpp:414, :527). When some RAPL zones are not readable it logs 'hw telemetry: N of M RAPL energy zones readable; ...' (src/pos/hwperf.cpp:529-535). The trace then holds counter tracks of the category hw. A failed thread start logs the warning 'hw telemetry: sampler thread not started (...)' (src/pos/hwperf.cpp:164).
variables.audience_reason: It only adds counters to Perfetto traces, and tracing belongs to developer-debug by the audience rules. A support engineer who captures a trace may set it.
variables.disagreement: cpp-pos-system.json names rinzler_proxy among the programs that read it. The code is linked into rinzler_proxy, but nothing there calls enable_hw_sampling: rinzler_proxy is built with RINZLER_NO_FUSE_MOUNT, so mount_fuse_stats is false and the capture worker is not started (src/rinzler.cpp:131-132, :4911). The SIGUSR1 tracer is installed only by the real libpos startup (src/pos/driver.cpp:447), not by pos_fake. src/rinzler.cpp never calls start_tracing. So the variable is never read in rinzler_proxy. Values, default and effect in the inventory agree with the code.

Every N seconds the thread writes one info log entry that starts with 'Latch states:' and lists the count and the name of every latch in the arena (h/tron/threading.hpp:223-246). A latch is a counter that threads wait on during a forward pass. Each model state owns one latch arena (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1240), so there is one watchdog thread per model state.

The comment at h/tron/threading.hpp:224 says CPU 0 is reserved for another program in production. variables.name: TRON_LIVE_TOKEN_LIMIT

readers.program: constructor of full_scheduler, in the full scheduler library (rinzler, runtron, rinzler_host through fake_scheduler_static, tests). Not in rinzler_proxy or rinzler_mock
readers.mechanism: std::getenv, used as the test for unset
readers.when: every call of the full_scheduler constructor

readers.program: constructor of full_scheduler (second call in the same expression)
readers.when: every call of the full_scheduler constructor

variables.values: Integer parsed with std::atoi into an int. Unit: live tokens (token jobs) in one forward pass. A useful value is 1 or more.
variables.default: Unset: 100000000 tokens (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1838). This is in practice no limit.
variables.empty_value: atoi gives 0. The result is the same as for an invalid value: the process aborts at the first forward pass that has work.
variables.invalid_value: The code does not reject any value. Non-numeric text gives 0. With 0 or a negative number, the check 'n_live_tokens >= live_token_limit' is true for the first token of every edge (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2410), so the pass gets no token job and reports that it did not schedule everything. forward() then fails TRON_ASSERT with the text 'Scheduler stuck: no work scheduled but not finished' (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2021-2025) and the process aborts. This result comes from reading the code. It was not run.
variables.effect: Sets the soft limit on the number of live tokens that one forward pass of a scheduler takes. At the limit the tree walk stops adding tokens to the pass (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2410-2413). The first K/V token of a page and a listener-only token are admitted only below the limit (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2191, :2543). A lower value gives smaller forward passes and more of them.
variables.interactions: When max_minibatches of the model config is above 0, the limit is the smaller of the variable and max_minibatches x max_minibatch_size (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:1839-1842). max_minibatches comes from rinzler -b / --max-batches (src/rinzler.cpp:4323-4325) or runtron --max-minibatches (src/runtron.cpp:969), merged with a bound from the model plugin (h/tron/models/config.hpp:112-118). The limit is soft: a page that already has K/V work is bound only by the hard capacity limit (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2181-2189). Each scheduler reads the variable when it is built. An EAGLE draft scheduler is a second scheduler and reads it again. The script bin/analyze-tps sets 100000 or 128 together with TRON_PER_USER_PROMPT_CHUNK_LIMIT to select a scheduling strategy (bin/analyze-tps:53-59).
variables.how_to_check: none found. No log line prints the limit. The Perfetto instant event 'forward args' of the category scheduler shows the number of token jobs of each pass (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2071-2074), which stays at or near the limit under load.
variables.audience_reason: It is a performance tuning value of the scheduler in rinzler and runtron, and a bad value stops the service.
variables.disagreement: Vague on the outcome of a bad value. cpp-tron.json says that with 0 or a negative value 'that loop adds no token to the pass' and stops there. The code goes on: build_forward_plan returns false with no token job, and forward() fails TRON_ASSERT 'Scheduler stuck: no work scheduled but not finished' (h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp:2020-2025). So an empty value, non-numeric text, 0 or a negative number aborts the process at the first forward pass that has a token to schedule. The document must state this. Parsing, default and effect agree.

Only a failed create or open ends the process. The inventory is also vague on the size: it gives the count argument 3, but the code keeps 3 rotated files next to the current file, so up to 4 files of 512 MiB (about 2 GiB) per directory. variables.empty_value: std::stoll throws std::invalid_argument. The process ends, as for an invalid value.
variables.invalid_value: Text that does not start with a number makes std::stoll throw std::invalid_argument. A number outside the 64-bit range throws std::out_of_range. Nothing catches the exception, and every caller of log_kv_footprint is noexcept (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:918, :1067, :1096, :1140, :1168, :1342-1346), so the C++ runtime calls std::terminate and the process aborts. This happens at the first call, which normally is the first KV book allocation, not at program start. 0 or a negative number is accepted and makes every call write a log line.
variables.effect: Sets how far the total KV cache size must move before the next info log line 'KV cache footprint: X.XX GB in N books' is written (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:599-608). The total is the sum over all KV books of the process. A line is written when the total differs from the last logged total by at least the value. A smaller value gives more log lines.
variables.interactions: The line is written at info level, so TRON_LOG_LEVEL above info hides it. The value is read once per process. No command-line flag sets it.
variables.how_to_check: The info log line 'KV cache footprint: X.XX GB in N books' (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp:608). The size step between two lines shows the value in effect.
variables.audience_reason: It controls the rate of a memory log line of a deployed rinzler, and a bad value ends the process.

variables.name: TRON_LOG_LEVEL

readers.program: libsystem, tron::init_logging(std::filesystem::path) (reached from rinzler, rinzler_mock, rinzler_host and rinzler_proxy at src/rinzler.cpp:4547, from runtron at src/runtron.cpp:439, and from the real libpos startup at src/pos/driver.cpp:198)
readers.mechanism: getenv. The text goes to spdlog::level::from_str (src/system/spdlog.cpp:43)

variables.values: One of these exact lower-case names: trace, debug, info, warn or warning, err or error, critical, off. The match is case-sensitive and the text is not trimmed. Source: spdlog v1.17.0, read from a local build copy at /home/jhan/workspace/tron/gen/_deps/spdlog-src (its version.h reports 1.17.0). The checkout pins v1.17.0 at cmake/versions.cmake:5 but does not hold the spdlog source (level::from_str in include/spdlog/common-inl.h:31-44).
variables.empty_value: The empty text is not a level name, so the level is off. No message is written to stderr or to the log file.
variables.invalid_value: Every text that is not one of the listed names gives the level off (spdlog from_str returns level::off). Examples: INFO, Debug, verbose, 'info ' with a space, 3. No warning is printed. With the level off, neither stderr nor the log file gets any message. This includes error messages and the message of a failed TRON_ASSERT, which is written with spdlog::error (h/common/assert.hpp:60-62).
variables.effect: Sets the lowest message level that TRON writes. The level is applied to the log file sink, to the stderr sink and to the default logger (src/system/spdlog.cpp:47, :50, :55).
variables.interactions: SPDLOG_LEVEL is applied after it (src/system/spdlog.cpp:60). In spdlog v1.17.0, load_env_levels changes only the level of the logger. The two sinks keep the level from TRON_LOG_LEVEL, and a message must pass both the logger level and the sink level. So the stricter of the two variables wins. SPDLOG_LEVEL can hide more messages but cannot show more than TRON_LOG_LEVEL allows. Example: trace output needs TRON_LOG_LEVEL=trace. SPDLOG_LEVEL=trace alone leaves the sinks at debug. Only the first call of init_logging reads the variable (static flag at src/system/spdlog.cpp:36-37). No command-line flag sets the log level (no set_level call outside src/system/spdlog.cpp in src/ and h/). The pos_fake startup does not call init_logging. Several tests read the same name with their own getenv (for example t/t_scheduler.cpp:35).
variables.how_to_check: none found. No log line prints the level in effect. A debug line such as the per-card 'caps { ... }' line (src/pos/device.cpp:337) appears only at debug or trace.
variables.audience_reason: It sets the amount of log output of every deployed TRON program, and a wrong name turns all log output off.
variables.disagreement: Vague. Both inventory files say the accepted names and the result of an unknown name were 'not determined', and that the way spdlog combines logger level and sink level was not determined. spdlog v1.17.0 answers all three. (1) The accepted names are trace, debug, info, warning, error, critical and off, plus warn and err. The match is exact and case-sensitive. (2) Any other text, the empty text included, gives the level off. The process then writes no log message at all, not even errors. (3) SPDLOG_LEVEL changes only the logger level. The sinks keep the TRON_LOG_LEVEL level. The stricter of the two wins. Source: spdlog v1.17.0, read from a local build copy at /home/jhan/workspace/tron/gen/_deps/spdlog-src (its version.h reports 1.17.0). The checkout pins v1.17.0 at cmake/versions.cmake:5 but does not hold the spdlog source. The default (debug) and the read time agree.

variables.name: TRON_LOG_PLACEMENT

readers.program: libtron, constructor of tron::hardware::placement_context (built during a model load at h/tron/models/model.hpp:1028; rinzler, runtron, rinzler_host, tests)
readers.mechanism: getenv. Only the null test is used
readers.when: every call of the placement_context constructor

variables.values: Any value turns it on. The text is not parsed. The values 0, false and off also turn it on.
variables.default: Unset: off. No placement count is kept and no line is written.
variables.empty_value: On. getenv returns a non-null pointer for an empty value, so an empty value differs from unset.
variables.invalid_value: There is no invalid value. Every set value turns it on.
variables.effect: Each placement context counts, per tensor name and per device, how many tiles it placed (src/tron/hardware/placer.cpp:144-149). When the context is destroyed, it writes one info log entry 'Tensor device counts: <JSON>' (src/tron/hardware/placer.cpp:38-47, :129). The JSON is indented, so the entry spans several lines. A placement context exists while model weights are placed on the FPGA cards during a model load.
variables.interactions: With the variable set, next_tile_devices also asserts that begin_tensor was called first (src/tron/hardware/placer.cpp:145-146). A call in the wrong order aborts the process with 'next_tile_devices used before begin_tensor' only when the variable is set. not determined: whether any product path calls in that order. The line is written at info level, so TRON_LOG_LEVEL above info hides it. No command-line flag sets it.
variables.how_to_check: The info log entry 'Tensor device counts: {...}' after each model load (src/tron/hardware/placer.cpp:47).
variables.audience_reason: It prints a diagnostic table of weight placement. It does not change placement.

variables.name: TRON_MAX_LOGITS_CHUNK_SIZE

readers.program: tron::init_logits_chunk_size, header code compiled into the full scheduler library (rinzler, runtron, rinzler_host through fake_scheduler_static, model tests). Not in rinzler_proxy or rinzler_mock, which link other schedulers
readers.mechanism: getenv inside a function-local static, then atol stored as size_t

readers.program: constructor of model::state (the caller that uses the value)

variables.values: Integer parsed with atol and stored as size_t. Unit: listeners (tokens that asked for logits) per chunk. A useful value is 1 or more. Text that starts with a number uses that number.
variables.default: Unset: the upper bound is 99999999, so the chunk size equals the number of workers of the application thread pool (h/tron/models/model.hpp:88-90). That pool has one worker fewer than the number of application CPUs (h/tron/threading.hpp:754-755).
variables.empty_value: atol gives 0, so the chunk size is 0. The result is the same as for the value 0: a division by zero in the first forward pass.
variables.invalid_value: The code does not reject any value. 0 and non-numeric text give a chunk size of 0. partition_listeners then divides by zero in every forward pass (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2058, :2161-2162). An integer division by zero is undefined behaviour in C++ and normally stops an x86 process with SIGFPE. This result comes from reading the code. It was not run. A negative number wraps to a very large size_t, so the chunk size is the number of pool workers, as when unset.
variables.effect: Sets an upper bound on the logits chunk size. The chunk size is the smaller of the value and the number of thread pool workers. At the end of a forward pass the listeners are handled in chunks of this size, one final matrix multiply per chunk (h/tron/models/model.hpp:3655-3698). The same number of pool workers send the listener notifications (h/tron/models/model.hpp:2134-2136). The chunk size also sets the length of the logits buffers of each model state (h/tron/models/model.hpp:1612-1613).
variables.interactions: The value can only lower the chunk size. It cannot raise it above the number of pool workers. The value is read once per process. No command-line flag sets it.
variables.how_to_check: none found. No log line prints the chunk size.
variables.audience_reason: It is a performance and memory tuning value of the inference path, and the value 0 stops the process.
